messages.content: What is the largest planet in the universe?

function.name: space_star_info

message.content:
The largest planet that astronomers have confidently identified so far is the protoplanet **HD 100546 b**. It orbits the young star HD 100546 and has a radius of roughly **2.5–3 times that of Jupiter** (about 0.25 R☉). Its mass is estimated to be a few times that of Jupiter as well, making it one of the most massive “planet‑sized” objects ever found.

> *Why it’s the biggest known:*  
>  - Most other “super‑Jupiters” discovered to date (e.g., WASP‑17b, HAT‑P‑32b) are only about 1–1.5 R_J.  
>  - HD 100546 b is still forming inside a circumstellar disk, so its size and mass are measured indirectly from the light it emits and the structure it creates in the disk.  

> *Caveats:*  
>  - Because it’s a protoplanet, its exact mass and radius are still being refined; future observations could revise these numbers.  
>  - There may be even larger planets out there that we haven’t detected yet—especially around very massive stars or in dense star‑forming regions where current surveys are less sensitive.

So, as of now, HD 100546 b holds the title for the largest confirmed planet in the universe.
